clue.text: Should formation include leading player who defends?

indicators.note: include means the rearranged letters take another letter inside them
a formation is an arrangement, so the letters of should are set out in a new order
leading picks out the front letter of the word player

explanation.surface: A football manager wonders whether the team shape should find room for a star defender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'formation' rearranges SHOULD to UHOLDS, and 'include' puts P, the first letter of 'player' (signalled by 'leading'), inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To uphold something is to support and maintain it, which is what someone who defends it does.

clue.text: Perhaps they favour love among convent's staff

parts.note: to be pro something is to favour it

indicators.note: among places the letter for love within the word for a convent member

parts.note: a nun is one of the people who make up a convent
love is nil in tennis scores, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Some nuns, it seems, are keen on romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' puts O inside NUN to make NOUN. 'Perhaps' says 'they' is just one example of the word class.
explanation.definitionFit: The word they is an example of a pronoun, a word standing in place of a noun.

clue.text: See 25
Outside left to cross over to divert shot

indicators.note: Outside says one piece wraps around the other, here the word for changing sides around the letter for left

parts.note: to defect is to cross over to the opposing side

explanation.surface: An outside-left crosses the ball, turning a shot away from goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside left' reads as a football position, but 'Outside' is the container signal: DEFECT goes around L.
explanation.definitionFit: To deflect a shot is to knock it off its course, turning it aside from its original path.

clue.text: Broken and heading for madness, leading player loses Donadoni's backing

indicators.note: heading for picks out the front letter of the word madness
player is read as something that plays with the letters of leading, rearranging them
loses says a letter is dropped from the word leading before it is rearranged
backing points to the rear letter of the name Donadoni

explanation.surface: Going mad, a star footballer has lost the support of his Italian teammate Donadoni.
explanation.walkthrough: 'player' looks like a footballer, but here it is the anagram signal. Roberto Donadoni was an Italian international footballer; the blog's commenters found this clue loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mangled has been crushed or damaged badly, so it is broken.

clue.text: Block opening attack, then lash out and start riot

indicators.note: opening takes the front letter of the word attack
out suggests the word lash is knocked out of shape and reordered
start takes the front letter of the word riot

explanation.surface: A defender blocks an attack, then loses his temper and starts a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Block' reads as a defensive action in football, but it is the definition: a block of dressed stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashlar is squared, dressed stone used in building, laid as blocks.

clue.text: Shifting, sliding as slippery semibreves

indicators.note: shifting means moving about, so the letters of sliding as are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: A musician describes notes that slide around as if on ice.
explanation.walkthrough: Commenters on the blog felt 'slippery semibreves' is loose: glissandi are slides between notes, not long notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Glissandi are musical slides from one pitch to another, so the notes in them slip along.

clue.text: Derby's No. 2 confirmed over alternative midfield? Not a pretty sight

indicators.note: over in a down clue places one piece above the next
No. 2 asks for the second letter of the word Derby

parts.note: yes is the word that confirms
or is the word that introduces an alternative
the middle of the word field is its third letter

explanation.surface: A Derby County player is confirmed for another midfield role, and it looks ugly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'midfield' is read as mid-field, the central letter E of FIELD. Derby County is an English football club.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyesore is something ugly to look at, so it is no pretty sight.

clue.text: Disquisitions degenerate into disasters

indicators.note: to degenerate is to fall into disorder, so the letters of into disasters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Long academic essays descend into catastrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: A disquisition is a long formal essay or discourse, the same thing as a dissertation.

clue.text: Spooner's heavy step to throw match here?

indicators.note: Spooner's means the opening sounds of two words are swapped, as Rev. Spooner reputedly did

parts.note: a bootfall is a heavy footstep, the sound of a boot landing
the second half of the word for a heavy footstep
to pitch is to throw

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a heavy-footed walk across the turf might lead to a fixed game.
explanation.walkthrough: BOOTFALL with its B and F swapped gives the first word; PITCH follows. 'throw match' suggests fixing a game, but 'match here?' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A football pitch is the field where a match is played, hence the question mark.

clue.text: "Beautiful game" quoted by leading journalist, referring to Beckham, usually on top

definitions.text: referring to Beckham, usually on top

indicators.note: quoted signals that the phrase is to be taken as said rather than written

parts.note: fair means beautiful, and the hare is game, an animal hunted for sport
ED, for editor, is the person who leads a newspaper's journalists

explanation.surface: A top writer cites football's nickname when describing David Beckham.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beautiful game' looks like football's nickname, but gives FAIR HARE, which sounds like FAIR HAIR. David Beckham is an England footballer usually seen with blond hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Beckham was usually blond, so describing his head of hair you would call it light-coloured.

clue.text: Miserable outside right is horny beast

indicators.note: outside means the beast's name wraps around the letter for right

parts.note: the moose is a large deer with big antlers

explanation.surface: An outside-right is described as a gloomy, horned animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside right' reads as a winger's position, but 'outside' puts MOOSE around R.
explanation.definitionFit: Morose means sullen and gloomy, the same mood as miserable.

clue.text: Attack on goal at end of game — it's caught by photographer

indicators.note: at end of places the attack piece after the game piece

parts.note: snap is a card game
a shot is an attempt to score

explanation.surface: A last-minute strike is captured on camera.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapshot is a quickly taken photograph, something a photographer captures.

clue.text: Home matches spoken of by backers

indicators.note: spoken of says the pieces are to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: in means at home, and vestas are short wax matches

explanation.surface: Home fixtures are talked about by financial supporters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'matches' suggests games but means VESTAS, wax matches; IN VESTAS said sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Investors put money into a venture, so they are its financial backers.

clue.text: Scored vital goal in match? Offside!

parts.note: to equal something is to match it
read as off side: off signals the letters of side are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A late equaliser in a match is disputed as offside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Offside!' splits into 'off' (rearrange) and 'side', giving ISED. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A team that equalised scored to level the game, often a crucial goal.

clue.text: Boatman! Gerbil-eating outrage!

indicators.note: eating means the words hold the answer within them, swallowed across the gap

explanation.surface: The setter, Boatman, exclaims at a scandalous gerbil.
explanation.definitionFit: Anger is the strong feeling that outrage also names, fierce displeasure.

clue.text: Defeat seen on television by right back

indicators.note: back means the combined letters are read from the end to the start

parts.note: the tube is slang for television

explanation.surface: A right-back's defeat is shown on TV.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns TUBER round. 'right back' reads as the defender.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebut an argument is to refute it, defeating it in debate.

clue.text: A lot of men have little weight to speak of

indicators.note: a lot of means most of, so one letter of men is dropped

parts.note: an ounce is a small unit of weight

explanation.surface: Many men are hardly heavy enough to mention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to speak of' looks like a set phrase; 'speak' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To enounce is to pronounce or state, which is to say words out loud.

clue.text: See 10
Cotton on cloth (an alteration)

indicators.note: an alteration is a change, here a change in the order of the letters of cloth an

explanation.surface: A tailor's note says cotton goes onto cloth as an alteration.
explanation.definitionFit: To cotton on is to understand, and to latch on means grasping an idea the same way.

clue.text: Leading player, coked-out, missing from action-packed game

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are taken apart and remade
missing from says the letters of coked are removed from the larger pool

explanation.surface: A team skipper, high on cocaine, misses an exciting game.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of COKED out of ACTIONPACKED; 'game' is a link. The left-over ATINPAC rearranges to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The captain leads a team on the field, its foremost player.

clue.text: See 25
Eye-shadow, rouge and bleached in tips and roots

parts.note: kohl is black eye make-up

indicators.note: tips are the first letters of the words rouge and bleached in

explanation.surface: A make-up list: eye-shadow, rouge, and bleached tips and roots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roots' reads as hair, but defines the vegetable; commenters noted it grows above ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Kohlrabi is a turnip-like vegetable grown for its swollen stem, loosely a root crop.

clue.text: Heavy-footed steps, public transport an afterthought

parts.note: a tram is a form of public transport
PS, postscript, is an afterthought added to a letter

explanation.surface: Someone plods along, then remembers the bus or tram.
explanation.definitionFit: Tramps are heavy, plodding steps, as in the tramp of marching feet.

clue.text: Fool gave West Ham a daft epithet

indicators.note: daft means silly, so the letters of fool gave West Ham a are thrown around

explanation.surface: A clown calls West Ham United by a silly nickname.
explanation.walkthrough: West Ham is a London football club. The resulting phrase is a football cliché.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a stock descriptive tag for football, an epithet applied to the sport.

clue.text: Two out of fourteen of Boatman's fixture hopes at first …

parts.note: Boatman is the setter, so his is one's, written without the apostrophe
a fixture is a scheduled event

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of the word hopes

explanation.surface: The setter hopes for a couple of wins in fourteen fixtures.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter calls himself 'one', so 'Boatman's' gives ONE'S.
explanation.definitionFit: Two fourteenths reduce to one part in seven, a simple fraction equivalence.

clue.text: … hosted by other means after Cantona finishes

indicators.note: after places the means piece behind the letter from Cantona
finishes picks the end letter of the name Cantona

parts.note: a way is a means of doing something

explanation.surface: The fixture is played on the other team's ground, once Eric Cantona finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: Read on from 26: an away fixture is one hosted by the other side. Eric Cantona was a French footballer.
explanation.definitionFit: An away game is played at the opponents' ground, so the other club is host.

clue.text: "Surveying for First Great Eastern lines," Yeats begins

indicators.note: First takes the opening letters of the words Great and Eastern

parts.note: odes are poems, lines of verse

indicators.note: begins takes the opening letter of the name Yeats

explanation.surface: A railway poster quotes W. B. Yeats on surveying the Great Eastern lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Geodesy is the science of measuring the earth's shape, the basis of large-scale surveying.

clue.text: They're not paid to report one after the other

indicators.note: to report is to say aloud, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: doing things in turns means one after the other

explanation.surface: Unpaid staff take turns making their reports.
explanation.definitionFit: Interns are trainees in work placements, often working without wages.
